subtopic: Moving to a new city on limited money
subtype: Approach: mental rehearsal of the daily commute before committing [Thinking]
passage: Ujjwal had two listings shortlisted in Bengaluru, one cheaper and further out. The thought of choosing on price alone felt wrong, so Ujjwal took a notebook and imagined a whole Tuesday in the cheaper place. Alarm at 6:10. Walk to the bus stop, wait. The crowded bus. Change at the junction. Office by nine, if the traffic was kind. Back at eight at night, the last stretch on an unlit road. Jeevan, an old college friend who lived nearby, said the buses thinned out after nine. On Sunday Ujjwal made the actual trip once, timing it. It took ten minutes longer than imagined, and the road really was dark. The cheaper flat no longer looked cheap.

qa.q: What time did the imagined alarm ring?
What did Ujjwal think about choosing on price alone?
qa.a: Ujjwal felt uneasy about it, and thought a full weekday should be pictured first to see the hidden costs.

qa.q: What could Ujjwal do next before deciding, and why?
qa.a: Ujjwal could try the evening trip once as well and count the cost of daily travel, because a hidden cost is only visible on the real route.

qa.q: How might Jeevan see Ujjwal's questions about the bus?
qa.a: Jeevan probably feels helpful as a local, and honest about the thinning buses, which is what Ujjwal needed to hear.

grounding: Before choosing a locality a person imagines a full weekday, including the commute and the return at night, and then tests the route once.
